claims.claimText: Warwick's AI Information Compliance Policy says all new uses of AI tools, products, or services must go through appropriate procurement processes, regardless of cost.
claims.claimValue: New AI tool uses require appropriate procurement processes

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Regardless of costs, all new uses of AI tools and services/products or services, must go through appropriate procurement processes.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: New AI tool or service uses must go through appropriate procurement processes regardless of cost.

claims.claimText: Warwick's student-facing guidance says students are required to state whether AI was used in the submission process and explain why, where, and how it was used.
claims.claimValue: Students must disclose AI use when used in submissions

evidence.evidenceSnippet: You will be required to state if any AI has been used as part of the submission procedure. If you use an AI, you must set out why, where and how you have done so.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Students must state AI use and explain why, where, and how it was used.
evidence.snippetLocation: Key principles for using AI / Declare it

claims.claimText: Warwick's AI Information Compliance Policy covers everyone with a contractual or implied relationship with the University and all information processed by the University.
claims.claimValue: AI information compliance policy applies to members and university-processed information

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The policy covers everyone who has a contractual (formal or informal/implied) relationship with the University, including employees, students, visiting academics, and consultants. The policy covers all information processed by the University, regardless of ownership or format.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: The AI information compliance policy applies to covered University members and University-processed information.

claims.claimText: Warwick's AI Information Compliance Policy says certain data, including personal or confidential material, University intellectual property, and some copyrighted or third-party data, must not be put into AI software without prior approval.
claims.claimValue: Restricted data must not be entered into AI software without prior approval

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Certain types of data must never be put into any AI software, without prior approval from IDG or the Research Ethics Committee. These include: Passwords and usernames. Personally identifiable information (PII) or other sensitive or confidential material. Any data related to University Intellectual Property.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Restricted data types must not be put into AI software without prior approval.

claims.claimText: Warwick's student-facing guidance says students may use AI only within requirements set out in assessment briefs and course handbooks, which may restrict or prohibit AI use.
claims.claimValue: Student AI use depends on assessment and course requirements

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The general position is that you can use Artificial Intelligence (AI) but must follow any requirements set out in assessments and course handbooks. Those requirements may restrict or prohibit the use of AI.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Student AI use is conditional on assessment and course requirements.
evidence.snippetLocation: Key principles for using AI / Check the rules

claims.claimText: Warwick's AI in research guidance says its principles apply to all researchers and researchers must consider AI-related research risks including integrity, information security, and accountability risks.
claims.claimValue: AI research guidance applies to all researchers and risk categories

evidence.evidenceSnippet: The principles set out in this guidance apply to all researchers as previously defined. Researchers must consider all risks that may be relevant to their research that arise from AI.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Warwick AI research guidance applies to all researchers and requires consideration of AI-related research risks.
evidence.snippetLocation: Who is expected to use this guidance / Risk Considerations

claims.claimText: Warwick's student-facing guidance tells students not to enter personal or confidential data into AI tools unless they understand what will happen to the data, and recommends Copilot chat with a Warwick account for that kind of data.
claims.claimValue: Student AI privacy guidance directs caution and recommends Warwick-authenticated Copilot chat

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Do not input any personal or confidential data into any AI tools, unless you fully understand what will happen to that data. The university recommends using Co-Pilot chat for this kind of data - when logged in with your Warwick account.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Students are told not to enter personal or confidential data into AI without understanding data handling.
evidence.snippetLocation: Key principles for using AI / Protect privacy

claims.claimText: Warwick's AI in research guidance says researchers are responsible for misconduct-type practices involving AI, including improper handling of information or use of another person's ideas, even if such practices occur inadvertently through an AI tool.
claims.claimValue: Researchers remain responsible for AI-enabled research misconduct risks

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Misconduct in research includes: the fabrication or falsification of research data; improper handling of information on individuals collected during research; or the use of another person's ideas, work or research data without appropriate acknowledgement. Researchers are responsible for any such practices, even if they occur inadvertently through the use of an AI tool.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: The research guidance keeps researchers responsible for AI-enabled misconduct-type practices.
evidence.snippetLocation: Breach of Responsibilities and Expected Standards

claims.claimText: Warwick's assessment-design guidance says generative AI use in student submissions needs thoughtful support so responsible use and clear demonstration of human achievement are maintained.
claims.claimValue: Assessment design guidance calls for supported responsible AI use

evidence.evidenceSnippet: use of generative AI technologies to produce text and other media as part of student submissions ... needs to be thoughtfully supported to ensure responsible use and clear demonstration of human achievements.
evidence.evidenceSnippetDisplay: Assessment guidance says AI use in submissions needs support for responsible use and clear human achievement.

claims.claimText: Warwick's responsible-use guidance frames responsible AI use as honest, ethical, transparent, human-accountable, safe, secure, and attentive to bias, fairness, inclusivity, and accessibility.
claims.claimValue: Responsible AI use principles emphasize human accountability, transparency, safety, and fairness

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Responsible use includes ... using AI with honesty, in ethical and defensible ways, with human responsibility taken for the outcomes; being transparent about AI use; making concerted efforts to maximise safe and secure use; using AI in ways that mitigate bias and promote fairness, inclusivity and accessibility.
